messages:
alice: Heads-up: hit a weird KV eviction spike on qwen-mqa during long-context chat replay. Looks tied to rope-phase shifts when we switch kernel variants.
ben: ugh. repro steps?
alice: Running a 100k token synthetic with intermittent short bursts (avg batch 8 -> spikes to 48). After ~45m memory grows and we see repeated slab churn + eviction of hot slots.
carla: Did you see the kernel handoff logs? We swapped from fused-mqa-compact -> generic-gqa at ~seq=16384 because kernel selector thought GQA would be cheaper.
alice: yup. when that handoff happens rope uses different phase normalization and KV alignment shifts by a word. Causes small offsets in page keys -> fragmentation + duplicate pages.
dan: can you paste the trace? even a short snippet helps.
alice: paste:```
[2026-03-14T10:12:03Z] kernel-select: fused-mqa-compact @gpu0
[2026-03-14T10:12:03Z] kernel-switch: candidate=generic-gqa reason=throughput_est
[2026-03-14T10:12:03Z] kv:write slot=0x7ffb3b length=4096 rope_phase=5
[2026-03-14T10:12:03Z] kv:write slot=0x7ffb3b length=4096 rope_phase=6
[2026-03-14T10:12:04Z] kv:evict slot=0x7ffb3b reason=fragmentation
[2026-03-14T10:12:04Z] kv:alloc slot=0x7ffb4a length=4096 rope_phase=6
``` 
carla: TL;DR we end up with duplicate slots because phase used in page key changed across kernels. eviction heuristics see higher churn and start evicting despite locality.
ben: telemetry-bot, any prometheus counters?
telemetry-bot: KV_evictions{model="qwen-mqa",region="us-west-2"} +342% (baseline window 1h -> spike localized to kernel-switch windows). avg_page_reuse_time increased x4.
alice: repro is deterministic on my bench. attaching small repro script:```
# minimal repro
run_infer --model qwen-mqa --seqs 16k,2k,2k,8k --batch-schedule spike --duration 45m
```
dan: interesting. Does it also happen on llama-mqa or only qwen?
alice: qwen shows strongest signal, llama-mqa shows small blip, mistral/gqa not reproducible (likely because their rope-phase logic is stable across kernels).
carla: hypothesis: kernel selector uses different rope normalization constants for MQA vs GQA variants. We should either canonicalize the rope_phase used for KV keys or include kernel-version in key namespace so we don't mix.
ben: including kernel-version in key namespace will bloat cache namespace and prevent reuse across benign switches.
dan: right. better to make rope_phase derivation deterministic and independent of transient kernel micro-choices.
alice: proposed quick fix: when kernel-switch is scheduled for a request group, delay switching until we flush or remap current prefix KV or apply a phase-rebase that rewrites keys in-place (cheap for small pages).
carla: phase-rebase sounds heavy but might be ok if we're only touching the small set of recently-written pages. We can do it as an async patch during graceful handoff.
ben: follow-ups:
- bencher: add synthetic with kernel switching pattern (alice)
- infra: add a selector-flag to prefer stable-rope-mode for MQA when long-prefix > 12k (carla)
- runtime: implement phase-rebase prototype and perf test (dan)
- telemetry: track kernel-switch windows and kv-dup-key counts (ben)
alice: I'll open a PR with repro + patch suggestion. putting rough perf numbers in the PR: before: evict_rate 0.9/s -> after (stable-rope) 0.12/s on same bench.
carla: also note this interacts with batching heuristics: large batch spikes cause selector to flip mode because of throughput predictions. we may need a hysteresis.
ben: add hysteresis + keep-alive for current kernel for N seconds after ramp-down.
dan: cool. filing incident ticket for the customers who hit this yesterday: tick-#9874.
alice: thanks all. I'll post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
